diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $R^\top_i$ denote the $i$th row vector of $\bm W^{\frac{1}{2}}\bm V$.
\bm U(\bm p) \coloneq \bm V^\top\bm W^{\frac{1}{2}}\bm\Sigma(\bm p)^{-1}\bm W^{\frac{1}{2}}\bm V

issues.failure_explanation: With $R_i^\top$ the $i$-th row of $\bm W^{1/2}\bm V$, the information matrix is $\bm U(\bm p)=Lm\sum_i \frac{p_i}{w(x_i)\sigma^2(x_i)}R_iR_i^\top$ (using the diagonal form of $\bm\Sigma(\bm p)^{-1}$). Hence a direction $\bm a$ with $\sum_i \frac{a_i}{\sigma^2(x_i)}R_iR_i^\top=0$ does not leave $\bm U$ (and thus the objective $H(\bm p)=\tr(\bm U(\bm p)^{-1})$) invariant unless $w$ is constant on the support; invariance requires the combination $\sum_i \frac{a_i}{w(x_i)\sigma^2(x_i)}R_iR_i^\top=0$. Moreover, nothing ensures $\sum_i a_i=0$, so $\bm q_n^*+t\bm a$ generally leaves the simplex $\mathcal P_m(\delta)$; the conclusion that the perturbation yields another optimal solution is therefore unsupported as written.

failure_location.quote: Applying a perturbation argument for $\bm q^{*}_n$ along $\bm a$ yields another optimal solution that has a smaller $\delta$-support.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the null combination with weights $1/(w(x_i)\sigma^2(x_i))$ (equivalently define $R_i$ as rows of $\bm V$), and add the standard feasibility argument: at an optimum the KKT gradient condition on $\supp_\delta$ together with the trace of the null combination forces $\sum_i a_i=0$ (or argue via Loewner monotonicity of $H$ that a null direction with $\sum_i a_i\neq0$ contradicts optimality); then move along $\pm\bm a$ until a coordinate hits $\delta$. This is the classical support-size argument for A-optimal designs and recovers \eqref{spt} unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The sparsity bound \eqref{spt} of Lemma mkjh is not established by the given proof. It is used only to interpret the sparsity of the reweighted allocation $\bm q_n^*$ (subsequent remark and the numerical experiments); no theorem depends on it.
issues.title: Perturbation argument for the support bound does not preserve the objective or simplex feasibility
issues.why_classification: The statement \eqref{spt} is correct (standard A-optimal-design support bound); the proof needs only a local correction of the perturbation direction plus a short standard feasibility argument, with no change to any claim, rate, or scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \tr(\bm U(\bm p)^{-1}),\quad\quad \bm U(\bm p) \coloneq \bm V^\top\bm W^{\frac{1}{2}}\bm\Sigma(\bm p)^{-1}\bm W^{\frac{1}{2}}\bm V
That is, for any other linear unbiased estimator $\widetilde{\bm\beta}$ for $\bm\beta$, $\Cov[\widehat{\bm\beta}]\preceq\Cov[\widetilde{\bm\beta}]$

issues.failure_explanation: Gauss--Markov compares covariance matrices: at fixed $\bm p$ it gives $H(\bm p)=\tr(\bm U(\bm p)^{-1})\le\tr\big((\bm V^\top\bm W\bm V)^{-1}\bm V^\top\bm W^{1/2}\bm\Sigma(\bm p)\bm W^{1/2}\bm V(\bm V^\top\bm W\bm V)^{-1}\big)$, the trace of the non-reweighted estimator's covariance, not $H(\bm p)\le G(\bm p)=\tr(\bm V^\top\bm W^{1/2}\bm\Sigma(\bm p)\bm W^{1/2}\bm V)$. The claimed inequality is false in general: take $\mu$ uniform on three points $\{a,b,c\}$, $V_2=\mathrm{span}\{v_1,v_2\}$ with $v_1=(\sqrt3,0,0)$, $v_2=(0,\sqrt{3/2},\sqrt{3/2})$, $\sigma^2=\Phi_2$ (so $J_n=1$), $m=3$, $\XX=\{a,b,c\}$; then $\bm p_n^*=(1/3,1/3,1/3)$, $G(\bm p_n^*)=4/L$ while $H(\bm p_n^*)=4.5/L$. Hence $\E_\XX[H(\bm q_n^*)]\le\E_\XX[G(\bm p_n^*)]$ is also not established.

failure_location.quote: it can be verified using \eqref{neyman} that $\bm p_n^*\in\mathcal P_m(\delta)$ so that $H(\bm q^{*}_n)\leq H(\bm p^*_n)\leq G(\bm p^*_n)$ (the first inequality follows from the definition of $\bm q_n^*$ and the second uses the Gauss--Markov theorem), which implies $\E_\XX[H(\bm q^{*}_n)]\leq \E_\XX[G(\bm p^*_n)]$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $H(\bm p_n^*)\le G(\bm p_n^*)$ by the correct Gauss--Markov consequence $H(\bm p_n^*)\le\tr(\Cov_{\mathrm{OLS}}(\bm p_n^*))$, or by the looser $\cond(\bm V^\top\bm W\bm V)^2 G(\bm p_n^*)$ (which is $\le\tfrac32 G(\bm p_n^*)$ on the event $\AA$), and restate the expectation comparison with that factor or conditionally on $\AA$.
issues.overall_effect: The quantitative justification in Remark rem:compare that the reweighted variant's variance term $\E_\XX[H(\bm q_n^*)]$ is dominated by the non-reweighted $\E_\XX[G(\bm p_n^*)]$ fails; the remark's interpretation of \eqref{p1-2} loses its supporting comparison. Theorem thm:main (both cases) does not rely on this remark, so no formal result inherits the defect.
issues.title: False inequality $H(\bm p_n^*)\le G(\bm p_n^*)$ attributed to the Gauss--Markov theorem
issues.why_classification: An isolated interpretive remark with no formal dependents; the repair is a local restatement of the comparison (Gauss--Markov applied to the OLS covariance, or an extra condition-number factor) that preserves the remark's qualitative conclusions and leaves all theorems untouched.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Choosing $l\geq \log(1/\delta)/\log 2$ and noting $2/\log 2<3$ yields the desired result.

issues.failure_explanation: The boosting needs $l$ disjoint blocks of $k$ basis functions, i.e. $lk\le n$, and failure probability $(1/2)^l\le\delta$, i.e. $l\ge\log_2(1/\delta)$; with integer blocks this requires $n\ge\lceil\log_2(1/\delta)\rceil k$, which $n>1.5\log(1/\delta)k$ does not imply. Example: $\delta=0.01$, $k=100$, $n=691$ satisfies $n>1.5\ln(100)\cdot100\approx690.8$, but only $l=\lfloor n/k\rfloor=6$ blocks fit, giving failure bound $2^{-6}=1/64>\delta$, while $l=7$ blocks need $n\ge700$. Thus for part of the stated regime the proof does not deliver the claimed $1-\delta$ probability.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the hypothesis as $n\ge\lceil\log(1/\delta)/\log 2\rceil k$, or use the clean sufficient form $n>1.5\log(2/\delta)k$ (which implies the former); the scaling $n\gtrsim \e^{-2}\|\sigma\|_{L^2_\mu}^2\log(1/\delta)$ and the error conclusion are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem thm:rb's explicit sufficient condition is not established for moderate $\delta$ and large $k$; as written the argument certifies the $1-\delta$ conclusion only under the stricter condition $n\ge\lceil\log_2(1/\delta)\rceil k$. The theorem serves as the baseline approximation-capacity result and is invoked in the numerical discussion.
issues.title: Boosting step does not cover the stated range $n>1.5\log(1/\delta)k$
issues.why_classification: The repair changes only constants/slack in the stated sufficient condition via the existing boosting argument; the conclusion, the rate, and the theorem's role all survive with no new lemma or construction.

issues.failure_explanation: For $r=1$, $(\log r)^3=0$, so $k=\lceil0\rceil=0$ and the hypothesis $n>10\log(1/\delta)k=0$ is vacuous. But $\bar V_{n,0}=\{0\}$ (only the zero coefficient vector has support size $\le0$), so the conclusion asserts $\|f\|_{L^2_\mu}\le24\sqrt{\tau_2}$ with probability $\ge1-\delta$ for every $\delta>0$, i.e. surely. This is false whenever $\|f\|_{L^2_\mu}>24\sqrt{\tau_2}$ (e.g. a large mean $f$ with arbitrarily small noise spectrum). The proof implicitly needs $\log r>0$ (it takes $s>2r+1$ and blocks of size $k\ge2s$), an omitted hypothesis.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis $r\ge2$ (equivalently define $k=\lceil C_1 r(\log(r\vee2))^3\rceil$).
issues.overall_effect: Theorem thm:984 as stated is false at the boundary value $r=1$; all content for $r\ge2$ (the meaningful spectral-tail regime) is unaffected.
issues.title: Degenerate case $r=1$ makes Theorem thm:984 false as stated
issues.why_classification: A standard exclusion of a degenerate parameter value; the method, conclusion, rate, and advertised scope (large $r$ with decaying kernel spectrum) are unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The single-block construction succeeds with probability $\ge0.1$ using at most $k$ basis functions, so lifting to $1-\delta$ requires $l$ disjoint blocks with $0.9^l\le\delta$, i.e. $l\ge\log(1/\delta)/\log(10/9)\approx9.49\log(1/\delta)$, and feasibility requires $\lfloor n/k\rfloor\ge l$. The hypothesis $n>10\log(1/\delta)k$ only gives $\lfloor n/k\rfloor>10\log(1/\delta)-1$, which is insufficient for moderate $\delta$: e.g. $\delta=0.5$, $k=20$, $n=139$ satisfies $n>10\ln2\cdot20\approx138.6$ but allows only $l=6$ blocks, giving failure bound $0.9^6\approx0.53>\delta$, while $l=7$ requires $n\ge140$.

failure_location.quote: The proof is finished by applying a similar boosting argument in Theorem \ref{thm:rb} to lift the constant probability in both cases to $1-\delta$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the hypothesis as $n\ge\lceil\log(1/\delta)/\log(10/9)\rceil k$, or use the clean sufficient form $n>10\log(2/\delta)k$; the rate $n\gtrsim r(\log r)^3\log(1/\delta)$ and the error bound $24\sqrt{r\tau_{r+1}}$ are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit sufficient condition of Theorem thm:984 is not established for moderate $\delta$ and large $k$; as written the proof certifies the $1-\delta$ conclusion only under a slightly stricter sample condition.
issues.title: Final boosting step does not cover the stated range $n>10\log(1/\delta)k$
issues.why_classification: Only constants/slack in the sufficient condition change, via the existing boosting argument; the conclusion, the $(\log r)^3$ rate, and the theorem's scope all survive without new proof architecture.
